device: NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Engineering Reference Developer Kit Super
clock_note: Diagnostic only. GPU DVFS was unlocked at 306-1020 MHz and CPU clocks were also unlocked. Results must be repeated under locked clocks before release acceptance.
objective: Identify the next material Orin optimizations without changing the DCVC-RT codec generation and without regressing x86 Linux or desktop RTX support.

balanced_abbaaa_benchmark.description: Balanced A-B-B-A-A-B diagnostic comparing A=dynamic 720p-fp16 bundle and B=fully fixed canonical bundle. Each encode was followed by matching decode and quality measurement.

correctness.note: Different target-local TensorRT FP16 tactics produced a different deterministic stream with negligible quality change. This is not a cross-runtime compatibility claim.

cuda_graphs.note: 540p is above the accepted integrated-device graph area cap.

balanced_abbaaa_benchmark.decision: Promote fully fixed, target-local TensorRT profiles to the first acceptance wave. Do not package them until locked-clock, multi-sequence, GOP-1/GOP-97, correctness, memory, and energy gates pass.

hot_path_profile.workload: 640x360 BasketballDrive, 9 frames, GOP 9, QP 32, warmed P frames
hot_path_profile.diagnosis: Steady-state Orin throughput is dominated by sequential TensorRT neural compute, especially p_synthesis, p_reference_feature, and p_analysis. CPU entropy, enqueue setup after CUDA Graph warm-up, allocations, and copies are secondary.

tensorrt_microbenchmarks.engine: dynamic 720p-fp16 p_synthesis.plan at fixed 360p input shapes
tensorrt_microbenchmarks.layer_profile_diagnosis: Work is distributed across decoder and reconstruction depth-convolution/FFN blocks; no single reformat or copy node dominates.

mlvc_audit.useful_runtime_lesson: MLVC explicitly exports fixed-resolution NPU models. This aligns with the measured benefit of fixed TensorRT profiles.
mlvc_audit.benchmark_semantics: The local MLVC benchmark derives encoder/decoder FPS from MLVC model inference timers. ModelWrapper.inference_time surrounds model.predict/infer only, while FrameLoopTotal separately contains the full loop and supporting work. NVCR complete codec wall-time FPS is therefore not directly comparable to MLVC's reported model FPS.
non_drop_in_changes: Scale sending changes entropy parameters and the bitstream, allowing one arithmetic decode pass instead of interleaving entropy and neural calls.
The recurrent feature width is reduced from 256 to 128.
MLVC-S is a substantially smaller 5.4M-parameter codec.
NPU-friendly activations, memory, unified I/P handling, long-term reference recovery, and the published rate-distortion results require training/model changes.
mlvc_audit.comparison_note: Published MLVC numbers use Apple, Intel, and Qualcomm NPUs and a different codec/model/timing scope. They are architectural evidence, not an Orin Nano DCVC-RT target.

ranked_next_waves.name: Accept and package canonical fully fixed 360p/540p profiles
ranked_next_waves.expected_gain_signal: Observed +20.342%/+7.748% encode/decode at 360p and +15.470%/+8.285% at 540p in unlocked-clock diagnostics.
ranked_next_waves.gate: Locked clocks and thermal logging; A-B-B-A-A-B; GOP 1 and 97; at least five sequences; three measured repetitions; exact payload/PSNR/reconstruction evidence; peak memory and energy; release tests and cross-runtime golden checks.
ranked_next_waves.compatibility: Resolution selection chooses a target-local plan only when model, target, TensorRT/CUDA, precision, and exact shape match. Dynamic plans remain the fallback. Orin plans are never loaded on RTX/x86.

ranked_next_waves.name: Search TensorRT tactics on fixed hot engines
ranked_next_waves.expected_gain_signal: Potential additional single-digit gain; fixed-shape tactic selection already produced the largest runtime-only improvement.
ranked_next_waves.scope: Probe p_synthesis, p_reference_feature, p_analysis, and p_prior independently using locked clocks, builder optimization level 4/5 where memory permits, controlled workspace sizes, zero/one auxiliary stream, detailed profiling, and target-specific timing caches. Promote only whole-codec gains above 3% with unchanged correctness.
ranked_next_waves.compatibility: Build and cache tactics independently per GPU target. No codec, public API, or x86 code-path change.

ranked_next_waves.name: Preallocate and bind ping-pong DPB outputs
ranked_next_waves.expected_gain_signal: Likely below 3% throughput but removes two allocations and 3.297 MB of allocation churn per P frame, stabilizes addresses for CUDA Graph replay, and reduces integrated-memory fragmentation risk.
ranked_next_waves.scope: Allow caller-provided output buffers in run_device_engine and retain two frame/feature DPB slots. Measure throughput, peak memory, and long-GOP stability.
ranked_next_waves.compatibility: Backend-local buffer-management change using existing CUDA semantics; retain the existing allocation fallback and test both integrated and discrete GPU policies.

ranked_next_waves.name: Accuracy-aware mixed precision only if more than 25% additional speed is required
ranked_next_waves.expected_gain_signal: Potentially material, but requires new trained artifacts. Prior PTQ delivered about 19-21% speed while catastrophically reducing PSNR to about 16 dB.
ranked_next_waves.scope: Sensitivity-guided Q/DQ and quantization-aware training focused first on hot reconstruction/reference FFN convolutions, with entropy-parameter networks retained in FP16 until proven safe. Consider structured 2:4 sparsity only with fine-tuning and rate-distortion validation.
ranked_next_waves.compatibility: Use a new model/artifact identity and explicit bitstream compatibility gate; retain the FP16 backend and desktop fallback.

deprioritized_or_rejected: Persistent L2 cache: neutral in the direct p_synthesis probe.
Broad multi-stream execution: the codec stages are mostly causally sequential, TensorRT adds synchronization events, and extra streams increase memory pressure.
More CUDA Graph work at 540p: graph launch overhead is small relative to neural compute and the current accepted policy intentionally caps integrated-device graphs at 360p.
More runtime-only fusion/compaction: prior reference/prior fusion gained only 1.10% and the two-way compaction kernel regressed.
INT8 PTQ: rejected for catastrophic rate-distortion failure.
DLA: Jetson Orin Nano has no DLA.
FP8: Orin Nano's Ampere GPU does not provide the newer FP8 Tensor Core path.
decision: The next implementation should begin with acceptance and resolution-aware use of the canonical fixed 360p/540p bundles. Follow with a hot-engine TensorRT tactic search. Buffer preallocation is worthwhile for robustness but is not expected to be the drastic throughput change. MLVC-style scale sending or smaller models belong to a separate codec/model generation, not this NVCR/DCVC-RT runtime optimization wave.
